html:
The first of the three great tragic poets of Athens, born around 525 BCE at Eleusis, home of the Eleusinian Mysteries. He is often called the father of tragedy.

He fought against the Persians at the Battle of Marathon in 490 BCE, where his brother was killed, and probably at Salamis ten years later. He won his first victory at the Dionysia in 484 BCE.

Aristotle says he added a second actor, so characters could speak with each other, not only with the chorus. He wrote perhaps 70 to 90 plays, of which seven survive, among them:

  • The Persians (472 BCE), about the Persian defeat at Salamis
  • the Oresteia (458 BCE), a trilogy that ends with the founding of a court to replace blood feud

He died at Gela in Sicily around 456 BCE. His epitaph, said to be his own, names his fighting at Marathon and not his plays. Sophocles and Euripides followed him.
